correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <ul> creates unordered lists (bulleted). Remember: "U" for "unordered" = bullet points without specific order.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

correct.details: <ol> creates ordered lists (numbered). Remember: "O" for "ordered" = numbers indicating sequence.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: Each list item goes inside <______> tags.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <li> tags contain list items. Every bullet point or number in a list is wrapped in <li> and </li>.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <li> tags contain list items. Every bullet point or number in a list is wrapped in <li> and </li>.

questions.question: <ol type="______"> creates lowercase letters (a, b, c).

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: type="a" creates lowercase alphabetical numbering. type="A" creates uppercase, type="i" creates Roman numerals.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: type="a" creates lowercase alphabetical numbering. type="A" creates uppercase, type="i" creates Roman numerals.

questions.question: Lists inside lists are called ______ lists.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Nested lists are lists within lists. They create hierarchy, like sub-points under main points.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Nested lists are lists within lists. They create hierarchy, like sub-points under main points.

questions.question: For a shopping list without order, use <______>.

correct.details: Shopping lists (no specific order) use <ul> (unordered list). Order doesn't matter for grocery items.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
